user.title: Add a kiosk panel
user.description: Install the pikioskd agent on the Raspberry Pi first (agent/install.sh in this repository). The installer prints the panel's remote-admin password once and stores it at /etc/pikioskd/settings.json.

data_description.port: The agent's remoteAdminPort. 2323 unless you changed it.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only for a self-signed certificate on your own LAN.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter the password
reauth_confirm.description: {host} refused the stored password. Re-provisioning a panel generates a new one; read it back from /etc/pikioskd/settings.json on the device.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the agent. Check the address and port, and that pikioskd is running (systemctl status pikioskd).
error.invalid_auth: The agent refused that password, or remote administration is switched off on the device.
error.unknown: The agent answered something unexpected. Check its journal: journalctl -u pikioskd.

agent_migration.title: {title} needs the kiosk agent installed
agent_migration.description:
Kiosk Pi 1.0.0 replaces the SSH transport with the pikioskd agent, which runs on the panel itself. Everything about this entry carried across except the password — the agent generates it on the device when you install it, so it did not exist until now.

1. Run `sudo agent/install.sh` on the panel (from this repository) and note the password it prints.
2. Home Assistant has already asked to reconfigure this panel. Answer that prompt with the password.

DO NOT add the panel again from Add Integration, and do not delete this entry. This entry still holds the panel's identity, so adding it again is refused as already configured — and deleting it would take the panel's device, its entities and every recorded row behind them with it. Reconfiguring keeps all of it.
